summary: The ~30% order-submit failure rate is a downstream symptom of the external exchange partner (exchange-api) failing behind exchange-gateway: exchange-gateway's own upstream error rate stepped 0.30%→40.87% and upstream latency 120ms→~9400ms at 10:58–11:00Z, before order-service's first 504 at 11:02:45Z (F14, F10, F15). exchange-gateway's logs show 5000ms connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example plus partner-generated HTTP 503s carrying the partner's own x-partner-request-id, proving the partner is reachable but slow/failing rather than a network/mesh break (F24, F25, F26, F27). order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) is coincidental: its 11:16Z rollback changed nothing (errors flat ~30-33%, p99 ~5.0-5.7s through 12:58Z), and the deploy minute itself was normal (F13, F15, G/F8). Confidence is high (0.78 per reviewed ranking); the residual uncertainty is only whether the partner's fault is partner-side overload vs partner-side network, since exchange-api has no telemetry (F19, F20).

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway's upstream dependency (external exchange partner, exchange-api) is failing — 504s cascade to order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange partner (exchange-api, node type 'external', owner 'vendor', has_telemetry:false) that exchange-gateway calls for placeOrder/quoteSnapshot began responding slowly and with HTTP 503 at ~10:58-11:01Z. exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate jumped 0.30%->40.87% and upstream_latency_ms 120ms->9400ms, its own error rate stepped to 22-25% (plateau ~44%) at 11:00Z, and order-service — which calls exchange-gateway's placeOrder — then propagated 504 Gateway Timeout at ~30%. The partner is slow-but-reachable (fixed 5000ms connect timeouts plus partner-generated 503s carrying x-partner-request-id), i.e. the partner's own application is answering.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: exchange-api (external exchange partner, upstream of exchange-gateway)

causal_chain.claim: The only node downstream of exchange-gateway is exchange-api, an external vendor endpoint with no internal service behind it [F19,F23]
exchange-gateway had zero deployments and zero config/flag changes in 09:00-12:59Z, so nothing on our side changed to break this hop [F21]

The earliest signal in the incident is exchange-gateway's OWN upstream metrics: upstream_error_rate 0.30%->40.87% at the 11:00Z bucket and upstream_latency_ms ~120ms->2385/9400ms in the 10:58Z bucket [F14]; log-side first upstream timeout at 11:01:25Z [F24,F29]

The partner is slow-but-reachable, not unreachable: timeouts are all at the fixed 5000ms connect timeout, and the partner returns HTTP 503s carrying its own per-request ids (x-partner-request-id), proving requests arrive and a partner-side app responds [F24,F25]

No connection-refused or DNS error signature exists anywhere in exchange-gateway's 10:40-12:59Z logs (both substring searches returned 0), and only a circuit-breaker-open WARN appears — exchange-gateway's resilience layer tripping on the partner's failures, not a local network error [F26,F27]
exchange-gateway's error rate steps to ~22-25% (plateau ~44%) at 11:00Z, ~2-4 min BEFORE order-service's first error at 11:02:45Z, and its step is NOT at the v2.15.2 deploy minute [F10,F11,F15,F17]
order-service's placeOrder calls to exchange-gateway return 504 Gateway Timeout after ~5.3s; all 349 errors share this single signature [F8,F9]
order-service shows no internal CPU/DB-pool saturation, so the latency originates at the downstream call not in its process [F16]
Rolling back order-service v2.15.2 at 11:16Z changed nothing (error rate flat ~30-33% and p99 ~5.0-5.7s through 12:58Z), so the deploy is coincidental [F13,F17]
The identical timeout+503 signature is still being emitted at 12:58:32Z (~2h sustained), independent of the order-service release lifecycle [F28,F17]

Recorded precedent HIST-103 ('Order failures during exchange partner outage', 504 on order submit, upstream timeouts) had root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side' — matching this upstream identity (lead only) [F6,F22]

assumptions: The external partner's degradation is due to a partner-side fault (overload/outage) rather than an egress-network problem on OUR side that also produces 503s from the partner — the partner-generated x-partner-request-id 503s strongly favor partner-side, but partner-side root mechanism is not independently observable (has_telemetry:false)
HIST-103 is a genuine precedent, not merely a surface-level symptom match

ranked_hypotheses.title: Network/mesh/infrastructure failure on the egress path between exchange-gateway and its upstream
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An infrastructure-level fault (service mesh, gateway networking, DNS, or the exchange-gateway edge) disrupted the egress path from exchange-gateway to its upstream, producing sustained 504s on that hop and cascading to order-service.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: shared network/mesh path between exchange-gateway and its upstream

causal_chain.claim: exchange-gateway's upstream_latency jumps to ~9.4s and upstream_error_rate to ~45% at ~10:58-11:00Z
The onset is a single sharp step, consistent with a discrete infra/mesh event rather than gradual load
All order-service errors are 504 timeouts on the exchange-gateway call, i.e. a connectivity/timeout symptom rather than an application error
order-service shows no internal saturation, so the fault is not in its process
An infra/mesh event occurred on the egress path that is not captured by get_deployments/get_config_changes

assumptions: An infra/mesh change occurred that is not captured by get_deployments/get_config_changes (explicitly listed as a gap; absence of a change record is being used as positive evidence, which is weak)
A mesh/DNS/egress fault would still allow the partner to return HTTP 503s with its own x-partner-request-id — which is inconsistent with a connectivity break
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The mechanism is actively contradicted. A mesh/DNS/egress fault produces connection-refused/DNS/no-route signatures, but substring searches for 'refused' and 'dns' over exchange-gateway's full log window return 0 matches (F26); instead every timeout is at the fixed 5000ms connect timeout and the partner itself returns HTTP 503s bearing its own per-request ids, proving requests reach the partner and a partner-side application responds (F24, F25). exchange-gateway also had zero deployments/config changes in the window (F21), so no infra change on our side is evidenced. H4's pivotal hop is an unsupported assumption and the hypothesis rests on the absence of a change record.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 regression (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service v2.15.2 release ('Add idempotency keys to order submit') introduced a defect in the submit path that caused ~30% of order submits to fail with 504s.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5333 changing the order submit path (idempotency-key persistence, retry-safe handler) was the only deployment in the 24h window [F1]
A defect in the new handler causes order submits to hang/fail
Hangs surface as ~5.3s p99 and 30% error rate on order-service [F7,F9]
Errors are reported as 504 Gateway Timeout on downstream calls [F8]

assumptions: A submit-path code defect could manifest only as outbound exchange-gateway 504s rather than an internal error or a distinct error signature
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error signature is exclusively 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 (placeOrder)' with zero internal 5xx (F8), there is no CPU/DB-pool saturation on order-service (F16), and — decisively — the rollback at 11:16Z produced no recovery whatsoever (error rate flat ~30-33% and p99 ~5.0-5.7s through 12:58Z, F13). exchange-gateway degraded ~2-4 min BEFORE order-service and its step is not at the deploy minute (F10, F15). Rejection rests on F13/F8/F10/F15/F16, not on the unverified precise deploy minute.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cfg-2290 (redis-cache TTL 5->4s) causing a shared redis-cache cold-cache / load regression
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The config change cfg-2290 on pricing-engine at 09:20Z shortened the quote-cache TTL on the shared redis-cache path, degrading the pricing path and a shared cache, which cascaded into latency/timeouts observed on order-service submit.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2290 changed pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20Z; it is the only config change in the window and touches the shared redis-cache-backed pricing path [F3,F5]
Shorter TTL increases cache misses / load on redis-cache
This degrades shared components used along order-service's dependency chain
order-service submit calls time out, producing 504s

assumptions: a 1-second TTL reduction (5s->4s, 20%) is large enough to cause a 35x latency step
pricing-engine/redis degradation would surface on order-service as exchange-gateway 504s
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Now directly falsified by telemetry: pricing-engine shows NO degradation in the onset window — error_rate flat 0.10-0.31% and latency_p99_ms flat 56-66ms across all 21 one-minute buckets around 10:58-11:10Z, with no step at 10:58Z or 11:00Z (F30). Also timing is wrong (cfg-2290 at 09:20Z, ~1h40m before the sharp 10:58-11:02Z step), the sole error signature is a 504 on the exchange-gateway placeOrder call (F8), pricing-engine is not on that path, and exchange-gateway's own upstream failed first (F14). Other exchange-gateway callers step at 11:02Z, after the 11:00Z exchange-gateway step (F35).

facts.statement: All 349 order-service errors in the incident window share exactly one signature: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'; there were zero order-service internal 5xx.
order-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% (flat through 10:49Z) to 30.8% in the 11:02Z bucket with the earliest ERROR log at 11:02:45Z, and p99 stepped ~150ms→~5340ms; onset was a single sharp step.
exchange-gateway degraded BEFORE order-service: error_rate ~0.2% through 10:51Z then 24.93% (max 45.46) in the 10:58Z bucket, p99 131ms→3017ms (max 5288) in the same bucket.

exchange-gateway's own upstream metrics failed earliest: upstream_error_rate flat ~0.30% through 10:50Z then 40.87% (max 46.7) at 11:00Z, and upstream_latency_ms ~120ms → 2385ms (max 9177ms) at 10:58Z then ~9400ms thereafter.

At 2-min resolution, exchange-gateway was normal at the 10:48Z v2.15.2 deploy minute (0.15%) and at 10:58Z (0.26%), stepping to 22.79% at 11:00Z; order-service's first errors appear one bucket later. The exchange-gateway failure precedes and is not coincident with the deploy minute.
Rolling back order-service v2.15.2 at 11:16:00Z did not restore success: error_rate stayed flat ~30-33% from the 11:01Z bucket through 12:58Z (max 35.57% at 12:43Z) with p99 ~5.0-5.7s.

order-service showed no in-process resource saturation: cpu_pct flat ~39-41% across 10:30-12:59Z and db_pool_in_use flat ~13-15 connections; the ~5.3s p99 matches the downstream exchange-gateway call timeout.

The only downstream node of exchange-gateway is 'exchange-api', a node of type 'external' owned by 'vendor' with has_telemetry:false; there is no internal service downstream that could be the failing upstream.

exchange-api has no telemetry of its own, so its health is only observable indirectly through exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency_ms metrics; no vendor status feed is retrievable from the monitoring tools.
exchange-gateway had zero deployments and zero config/feature-flag changes in 09:00-12:59Z, so neither its own release nor a config change explains its upstream degradation.

exchange-gateway's WARN+/ERROR logs for 10:40-12:59Z (471 entries) are dominated by 'upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' for op=placeOrder (163, first_seen 11:01:25Z) and op=quoteSnapshot (146, first_seen 11:01:43Z), every one at the fixed 5000ms connect timeout — slow-but-reachable upstream, not immediate connect failure.

A second upstream error class exists: 'exchange-api returned <n> Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=<n>)' appears 161 times (first_seen 11:02:20Z), proving the request reached the partner and a partner-side application responded.

No connectivity-class signature exists in exchange-gateway logs for 10:40-12:59Z: contains='refused' returned total_matched=0 and contains='dns' returned total_matched=0 over the full window, actively discriminating against a network/DNS/mesh connectivity failure.

exchange-gateway's circuit breaker opened on the upstream: 'circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)' at 11:03:26Z, ~2 min after the first upstream timeout — its resilience layer tripped on the partner's failures, not a local network error.

The sustained condition is independent of the order-service release lifecycle: exchange-gateway's high-error plateau continued uninterrupted from 11:00Z to 12:58Z (42-47% per bucket) and the identical timeout+503 signature was still being emitted at 12:58:32Z.

pricing-engine (the cfg-2290 change target) showed no degradation in the onset window: error_rate flat 0.10-0.31% and latency_p99_ms flat 56-66ms across all 21 one-minute buckets around 10:58-11:10Z, with no step at 10:58Z or 11:00Z.

api-gateway and market-data-service (both callers of exchange-gateway) stepped at 11:02Z — after exchange-gateway's 11:00Z step and coincident with order-service's first error — indicating a common downstream fan-out rather than a shared 10:58Z upstream onset.

The stored precedent HIST-103 (2025-10-21, 'Order failures during exchange partner outage') matches this signature — '504 on order submit' and 'upstream timeouts', root cause external exchange API outage, resolution failover to a secondary exchange route — and matches the current upstream identity.

The only deployment in the 24h window before onset was order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) at 10:48:00Z, rolled back at 11:16:00Z; the only config change was cfg-2290 on pricing-engine (cache.ttl_seconds 5→4) at 09:20:00Z.
The shared components expose no error_rate metric (redis-cache, ledger-db, kafka), so the cfg-2290/redis hypothesis cannot be tested via error_rate on those components.

assumptions: The external partner's degradation is due to a partner-side fault (overload/outage/partner-side network) rather than an egress-network problem on our side that also happens to produce partner-tagged 503s; the partner-generated x-partner-request-id 503s and the absence of any connectivity-class error strongly favor partner-side, but the partner's own root mechanism is not independently observable because exchange-api has has_telemetry:false.
HIST-103 is treated as a supporting precedent for the same component (external exchange partner), not as independent evidence about the current incident.

The exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency_ms metrics are attributed to the exchange-api edge (the only downstream node), which is a reasonable reading of the dependency graph rather than a directly labeled metric dimension.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Logs and metrics agree the failure lies on exchange-gateway's call to api.exchange-partner.example, with the log evidence pointing to a slow/failing-but-reachable partner rather than a connectivity/DNS/mesh fault.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-2290 on pricing-engine (cache.ttl_seconds 5→4) — the only config change in the window; later shown to be a red herring.
order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) deployed by a.khan — the only deployment in the 24h window. exchange-gateway's error_rate is fully normal (0.15%) at this exact minute.

exchange-gateway begins degrading: p99 131ms→3017ms, error_rate 24.93% (max 45.46) in the 10:58Z bucket; upstream_latency_ms jumps to 2385ms (max 9177ms). order-service still normal at 10:58Z (0.26%).
exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate jumps to 40.87% (max 46.7) and its own error_rate steps to 22.79% — the earliest clear failure step, ~4 min before order-service's first 504.
Earliest upstream log signal: 'upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' (and op=quoteSnapshot at 11:01:43Z).
order-service error_rate steps to 30.8% and p99 to ~5340ms; api-gateway and market-data-service also step at 11:02Z (after exchange-gateway's 11:00Z step).
New distinct error class appears: 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=<n>)' — the partner itself answers with its own per-request id.
Earliest order-service ERROR log: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'.
exchange-gateway circuit breaker opens on the upstream: 'circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)'.
Incident reported by on-call SRE; order-service submit failure rate ~30%, 504s on order submit.
order-service v2.15.2 rollback completes — no recovery: error_rate stays ~31.59%, p99 5371.52ms.

Identical signature still being emitted ~2h after onset (e.g. 'exchange-api returned 503 ... x-partner-request-id=b62798d4'; 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms ... op=quoteSnapshot'); order-service error_rate still ~30.46% and p99 ~5202ms.

recommended_actions.action: Fail over exchange-gateway's exchange-api route to the secondary exchange route (the mitigation recorded for HIST-103) and open a priority escalation with the exchange-api vendor (owner 'vendor') with the concrete evidence: partner-generated 503s carrying x-partner-request-id (e.g. 46ed2490, e132511b, b62798d4) and >5000ms connect times to api.exchange-partner.example since ~10:58Z.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failing hop is exchange-gateway → external exchange-api (F19, F23, F24, F25); nothing on our side mitigates it, and HIST-103 shows route failover + vendor fix resolved the identical signature (F6, F22).

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating dep-5333 as the fix: confirm the order-service v2.15.2 rollback (already completed at 11:16Z) is not expected to change error rates, and keep v2.15.2 or re-ship it on merit rather than as a remediation. Do not revert cfg-2290 as a mitigation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback produced zero recovery (errors flat ~31% and p99 ~5.3s through 12:58Z), and pricing-engine shows no degradation at all in the onset window, so both changes are coincidental (F13, F30).

recommended_actions.action: Verify the mitigation by confirming recovery on exchange-gateway's own upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms (should fall from ~45-47% and ~9400ms toward the ~0.30%/120ms baseline), then order-service error_rate and p99 returning toward ~0.2%/~150ms, and the disappearance of the 'exchange-api returned 503' and 'upstream connect timeout' log lines.
recommended_actions.rationale: The causal chain was established through exchange-gateway's upstream metrics and logs; the same signals are the correct success criteria (F14, F24, F25, F28).

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms (e.g. page when upstream_error_rate >5% for 2 minutes) so partner degradation is detected before it propagates to order-service's 504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: exchange-gateway's upstream metrics stepped ~4 minutes before order-service's first error but no alert fired until the customer-visible 30% failure rate (F14 vs F8).

recommended_actions.action: Reduce exchange-gateway's placeOrder/quoteSnapshot connect timeout from the fixed 5000ms and tune the circuit breaker (currently opening only after ~2 min at failure ratio 0.47) so the caller fails fast instead of propagating ~5s 504s across order-service, api-gateway and market-data-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: Every upstream error sat at the fixed 5000ms connect timeout and the breaker tripped ~2 min after the first timeout, driving the ~5.3s p99 on all callers (F24, F27, F9, F35).

recommended_actions.action: Maintain a warm failover path to a secondary exchange venue with periodic health checks, and track a vendor-SLA/partner-health signal for exchange-api given it has no telemetry in our stack.
recommended_actions.rationale: The external partner has has_telemetry:false so its health can only be inferred from our own metrics, and the same partner-side failure mode has now recurred (F20, F6, F22).

recommended_actions.action: In the post-mortem, explicitly document that the reported suspicion (order-service release) and the cfg-2290 TTL change were both excluded by evidence, to prevent future mis-triage of this signature.
recommended_actions.rationale: The reporter suspected the release and the on-call began a rollback that could not help; the window contained dep-5333 and cfg-2290 as the only two changes, both coincidental (F1, F3, F13, F30).

data_gaps: exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false, so the partner's own health, status metrics and any vendor incident notice could not be retrieved; its state is inferred only from exchange-gateway's upstream_* metrics and logs (F19, F20). This is why the H2 sub-variant (partner overload vs partner-side network vs full partner outage) remains unresolved.
No partner-side logs were available (only exchange-gateway's view of api.exchange-partner.example), so the reason the partner returns 503s and takes >5000ms to connect cannot be confirmed directly.

Budget-exhausted queries left redis-cache (hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min), ledger-db (replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), kafka (under_replicated_partitions) and api-gateway latency_p99_ms unqueried for the 10:50-11:10Z window; the shared non-HTTP components' health during onset is therefore unverified (F34 notes they expose no error_rate at all).

The 'refused'/'dns' substring searches are not exhaustive tests for every mesh/network error class (e.g. 'no route to host', TLS handshake failures, envoy 'upstream connect error'); H4 is strongly disfavored but not exhaustively excluded by string search, though the partner-generated x-partner-request-id 503s independently prove requests reach a responding partner app (F25, F26).

The exact deploy/restart timestamp of order-service v2.15.2 was not retrieved; this does not affect the conclusion because the rollback-with-no-recovery result already excludes the deploy as causal (F13).

market-data-service and api-gateway were not checked beyond 11:10Z, so the duration of their 11:02Z step is unknown; blast radius beyond order-service/exchange-gateway/api-gateway/market-data-service is not fully enumerated.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that exchange-gateway's requests never reached the partner — e.g. connection-refused, DNS-resolution or mesh/egress error strings (or envoy 'upstream connect error') in exchange-gateway logs for 10:40-12:59Z — would move the conclusion from H2 (partner fault) toward H4 (network/mesh/egress fault on our side).
A vendor status feed or partner-side telemetry showing exchange-api healthy while our connects time out would indicate the fault is on our egress path rather than partner-side.
Discovery that exchange-gateway had an undetected deployment or egress/network configuration change in 09:00-12:59Z would reopen the infra-explanation branch.

Correlation showing pricing-engine/redis-cache (cfg-2290), ledger-db or kafka actually degraded in the 10:50-11:10Z window would reopen the shared-component hypotheses, though the exclusive exchange-gateway placeOrder 504 signature and pricing-engine's flat metrics currently exclude them.

Recovery of order-service error rates immediately upon the v2.15.2 rollback (which did not occur) would have implicated the deployment; conversely, data showing order-service failed before exchange-gateway's 10:58Z onset would invert the causal direction.

findings.statement: Across ALL services, exactly one deployment occurred in the 24h window before onset: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z by a.khan, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit', changed the order submit path ('Idempotency-Key header persisted in orders table', 'retry-safe submit handler'). It was rolled back at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z.

refs.quote: Add idempotency keys to order submit

findings.statement: Onset timing: the deployment was at 10:48:00Z and the incident window opens with the report at 11:10:00Z (~22 min after deploy); the rollback completed at 11:16:00Z (~6 min after the report). The '2-24h before onset' window contains only this deployment plus one config change.

Across ALL services, the only config/flag change in the window is cfg-2290 on pricing-engine: key 'cache.ttl_seconds' changed 5 -> 4 at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z by config-bot ('Shorter quote cache TTL'). pricing-engine is a direct HTTP dependency of order-service, and had no deployments in this period (count 0).

order-service dependency graph (caller -> callee): order-service -> ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http), kafka (queue-produce); api-gateway -> order-service. Shared components order-service depends on (used by several services) are ledger-db, redis-cache and kafka — flagged shared:true.

Shared-component overlap via pricing-engine: pricing-engine -> market-data-service (http) and pricing-engine -> redis-cache (cache). So redis-cache is shared between order-service's pricing-engine path and market-data-service; market-data-service has no direct edge to order-service. The cfg-2290 TTL change (5s->4s) sits on this redis-cache-backed pricing path, which is the only change touching a shared component near onset.

Historical precedent for this signature exists: HIST-103 (2025-10-21) 'Order failures during exchange partner outage' has the same symptoms ('504 on order submit', 'upstream timeouts') on order-service/exchange-gateway with root cause an external exchange API outage (match_score 3). Other timeout/504 precedents are HIST-102 (ledger-db failover), HIST-107 (redis cold-cache storm), HIST-116 (api-gateway envoy upgrade, '504 at gateway'), and HIST-110/HIST-115 on order-service itself. These are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

refs.quote: External exchange API outage on the partner side

findings.statement: order-service error_rate was flat at ~0.2% through 10:49Z and jumped to 30.8% in the 11:02Z bucket; the earliest ERROR log is at 11:02:45Z. Onset is a single sharp step, not gradual.

All 349 order-service errors in the window share one signature: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'. The failure is a downstream timeout on the placeOrder call to exchange-gateway, not an order-service internal 5xx.

refs.quote: exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder) orderId=07fcb25a

findings.statement: order-service p99 latency was ~150ms through 10:49Z and stepped to ~5340ms in the 11:02Z bucket (35x), consistent with the 504 timeouts. order-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~13-15 connections across the whole window (10:30-12:59Z), so there is no evidence of DB connection-pool exhaustion on order-service.

exchange-gateway degraded BEFORE order-service: its error_rate was ~0.2% through the 10:51Z bucket then rose to 24.93% (max 45.46) in the 10:58Z bucket, and its p99 went from ~131ms to 3017ms (max 5288) in that same 10:58Z bucket - both earlier than order-service's first error at 11:02:45Z.

exchange-gateway sustains a steady high error plateau (~44% avg, max 48.42) and p99 ~5000-5500ms from 11:05Z through at least 12:57Z, and exposes dedicated upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms metrics - i.e. exchange-gateway itself has an upstream dependency that was not yet inspected. Its own error plateau begins slightly before order-service's first 504.

Interpretation: order-service's ~30% error rate is a downstream-timeout symptom of exchange-gateway being slow/failing (504s), not evidence that the order-service v2.15.2 release is the origin. exchange-gateway's onset (10:58Z bucket) precedes order-service's first error (11:02:45Z), so the direction of causation points downstream/into exchange-gateway's own upstream.

Rolling back order-service v2.15.2 at 11:16:00Z did NOT restore the success rate: order-service error_rate stays flat at ~30-33% continuously from the 11:01Z bucket through the end of data (12:58Z avg 30.46%, max 35.57% at 12:43Z) with the finest 2-min resolution showing 31.59% at 11:16Z and 31.00% at 11:18Z - no drop after the rollback. p99 latency likewise stays at ~5.0-5.7s (11:16Z 5371.52ms, 12:58Z 5202.34ms). The deploy is therefore coincidental, not causal.

exchange-gateway's own upstream dependency failed FIRST and is the earliest signal: its upstream_error_rate was flat ~0.30% through the 10:50Z bucket then jumped to 40.87% (max 46.7) in the 11:00Z bucket and stayed ~45-47% through 12:50Z; its upstream_latency_ms jumped from ~120ms (10:54Z avg 119.91) to 2385ms (max 9177ms) in the 10:58Z bucket and ~9400ms thereafter. This upstream degradation begins at/before the exchange-gateway error onset and ~4 min before order-service's first 504.

Ordering of events at the deploy/onset boundary (2-min resolution): exchange-gateway error_rate is fully normal at 10:48Z (0.15%, the exact v2.15.2 deploy minute) and 10:58Z (0.26%), then steps to 22.79% at 11:00Z. order-service first errors appear one bucket later (11:01Z avg 21.04%). So exchange-gateway's failure precedes order-service's by ~2-4 minutes and its step is NOT at the deploy minute.

order-service shows no in-process resource saturation: cpu_pct is flat ~39-41% across 10:30-12:59Z (11:00Z avg 39.78, 11:10Z 40.08, 12:50Z 39.02), alongside the already-established flat db_pool_in_use ~13-15. The failure is not internal CPU/DB-pool exhaustion; the ~5.3s p99 matches the downstream exchange-gateway call timeout rather than any internal latency.

exchange-gateway's high-error plateau continues uninterrupted from 11:00Z to 12:58Z (every 4-min bucket between 42-47%, e.g. 12:58Z avg 45.13%) and its upstream_error_rate similarly persists at ~45-47% through 12:50Z - so the condition is sustained and independent of the order-service rollback or release lifecycle.

Interpretation: the failing latency originates DOWNSTREAM of order-service, in order-service's call to exchange-gateway, which is itself timing out on its own upstream. order-service is a victim propagating 504s; the v2.15.2 deploy and the pricing-engine cfg-2290 TTL change are both coincidental with respect to this onset, and rollback is not a remediation.

exchange-gateway's resolved upstream dependency is 'exchange-api', a node of type 'external' owned by 'vendor' with has_telemetry:false. The edge is 'exchange-gateway' -> 'exchange-api' kind 'external'. This is the external exchange partner, not an internal service.

exchange-api has no telemetry of its own (has_telemetry:false), so its direct health/status metrics and any vendor incident notice are NOT retrievable from the monitoring tools; its status is only observable indirectly through exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency_ms metrics.
exchange-gateway had zero deployments and zero config/feature-flag changes in 09:00-12:59Z, so neither its own release nor a config change explains its upstream degradation.

Recorded precedent HIST-103 (2025-10-21) 'Order failures during exchange partner outage' on order-service + exchange-gateway has symptoms '504 on order submit', 'upstream timeouts' and root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', resolution 'Failed over to secondary exchange route; partner fixed'. This is the stored precedent for an external exchange partner being the failing component, matching the current upstream identity. (lead only)

exchange-gateway's WARN+/ERROR logs from 10:40-12:59Z contain 471 entries (470 ERROR, 1 WARN), all clustered on a single upstream host: the dominant patterns are 'upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' (163, first_seen 11:01:25Z) and '... op=quoteSnapshot' (146, first_seen 11:01:43Z). Every timeout is at the fixed 5000ms connect timeout, i.e. slow-but-reachable upstream, not an immediate connect failure.

findings.statement: A second, distinct upstream error class is present: 'exchange-api returned <n> Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=<n>)' appears 161 times, first_seen 11:02:20Z. The upstream PARTNER (exchange-api) is answering with HTTP 503 and returning its OWN per-request id (e.g. x-partner-request-id=46ed2490, e132511b), which proves the request reached the partner and a partner-side application responded - inconsistent with a network/DNS/mesh connectivity failure to the partner.

No connectivity-class error signature exists in exchange-gateway logs for 10:40-12:59Z: a contains='refused' query returned total_matched=0 and a contains='dns' query returned total_matched=0, both over the same full window (data_range 07:00-12:59Z). This actively discriminates against H4 (connection refused / DNS / mesh/upstream connect failure): such a fault would surface these strings.

Only one WARN was emitted: a circuit breaker opening on the upstream - 'circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)' at 11:03:26Z, ~2 min after the first upstream timeout (11:01:25Z), showing exchange-gateway's own resilience layer tripped on the partner's failures rather than on any local network error.

pricing-engine shows NO degradation in the 10:50-11:10Z window: error_rate is flat between 0.10% and 0.31% (10:58Z avg 0.14, 11:00Z avg 0.26, 11:02Z avg 0.15) and latency_p99_ms is flat between 56.22ms and 66.38ms across all 21 one-minute buckets (10:58Z avg 63.66ms, 11:02Z avg 66.38ms). market-data-service p99 latency is flat 38.02-42.65ms across the entire 10:50-11:10Z window (10:58Z avg 42.4ms, 11:02Z avg 38.25ms, 11:10Z avg 38.8ms) - no latency step at 10:58Z or 11:00Z despite its error_rate rising at 11:02Z, so its errors are not latency-driven.

Its onset (11:02Z) is later than exchange-gateway's 11:00Z step and simultaneous with order-service's 11:02:45Z first error.

The shared components expose no error_rate metric at all; their actual metric sets are redis-cache: [connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct]; ledger-db: [connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min]; kafka: [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions]. So an error_rate comparison for redis-cache/ledger-db/kafka is not possible and must be done on those named metrics.

Two of exchange-gateway's sibling callers show a step (api-gateway, market-data-service) but both at 11:02Z, strictly after exchange-gateway's 11:00Z error step and at the same minute as order-service's first 504 - consistent with a common downstream fan-out rather than a shared 10:58Z upstream onset; pricing-engine (also in the same dependency cluster) shows no step at all. This argues against a broad mesh/infra origin (H4) affecting all callers, and localizes the fault to exchange-gateway's own upstream path.
